https://bnn-news.com/temperatures-in-lat.text: Baltics Social Politics Money Interviews Opinions In Focus World Leisure Advertising Baltics Social Politics Money Interviews Opinions In Focus World Leisure Advertising Home Baltics Latvia Latvia Social Temperatures in Latvia to climb to as high as +30°C midweek BNN August 5, 2026 Facebook Twitter Photo: BNN Temperatures in Latvia are expected to reach +30°C in some parts of the country by midweek, according to the Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre. On Wednesday, the 5th of August, skies will be mostly clear overnight, with cloud cover increasing during the day. Despite the additional clouds, no precipitation is expected. Winds will remain light, creating favourable conditions for patchy fog to develop overnight in some areas. Night-time temperatures will fall to +12°C to +17°C, with parts of northern Kurzeme and Vidzeme cooling to around +10°C. During the day, temperatures will rise to +25°C to +30°C, while coastal areas of Kurzeme will remain slightly cooler at +23°C to +24°C. On Thursday, skies will be partly cloudy. Brief showers are expected in some western and eastern areas during the morning, while eastern Latvia may also experience short-lived rain showers during the afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms are also possible. Winds will remain light, although light to moderate southwesterly to westerly winds will develop along the coast. Overnight temperatures will range between +17°C and +21°C, while daytime highs will reach +25°C to +30°C. Western Latvia and many coastal areas will be slightly cooler, with temperatures between +20°C and +25°C. On Friday, variable cloud cover will persist. Rain is expected overnight in parts of southeastern Latvia, with thunderstorms also possible. During the day, light rain will spread across most of the country. Light to moderate southwesterly to westerly winds will prevail, becoming gusty from Friday morning in western and central regions. Overnight temperatures will range from +14°C to +18°C, while daytime highs will fall to +18°C to +23°C. Over the weekend, skies will often remain cloudy, although sunny intervals are expected. Periods of rain will affect different parts of the country from time to time. A cooler air mass will begin moving into Latvia from Friday, keeping weekend temperatures between +18°C and +23°C. Weather conditions at the beginning of next week are expected to remain similar to those forecast for the weekend. By Ruth Comerford Â and Â Ghoncheh Habibiazad Published 30 August 2026 Updated 2 hours ago US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak island, a US official said, marking the first known American strikes on Iran since late July. "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz," the BBC's US partner CBS News quoted US Central Command (Centcom) spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins as saying. The IRGC said Sunday's attack killed and wounded several people, and vowed "response and punishment". It later said it had launched an attack on US military targets in Jordan, according to Iranian state media. The BBC has approached Centcom for comment. How the US could try to seize Iran's Kharg Island Published 30 March US plans to cut off military aid to key Middle East ally, BBC told Published 2 days ago Iran says it is 'fully prepared' to counter widened US economic sanctions Published 5 days ago Jordan's army said shortly after the IRGC statement that it had intercepted eight missiles. "Air defense systems intercepted eight missiles that breached the Kingdom's airspace at dawn today, Monday," Jordan's armed forces said in a statement, quoting the army's spokesperson, reported by the state Petra News Agency. The US strike is the first known attack on Iran since President Donald Trump paused a renewed military campaign in late July. Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global shipping. Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (Â£1.5m) to cross. Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields". Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said. Hours later, Iranian media carried a statement by the IRGC saying it had attacked the US bases of King Hussein and al-Azraq in Jordan with ballistic missiles in response to the Larak Island attack. The IRGC said it had caused "heavy damage" and targeted "technical infrastructure, maintenance facilities, and enemy fighter jet positions", according to a translation from the AFP news agency. Trump âsaid last week that all minesâ placed in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran as part of its efforts to blockade the route had been detonated or removed. He said Iran had been warned that any ship âor boat deploying new mines would be âdestroyed. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described Trump's claim as a "propaganda" deception. Iran is facing renewed economic pressure after Washington announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies . Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict. The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Iran war has now crossed its six-month mark. Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel through before the war began. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/10/lige.text: Menü Kereső Ligeti Miklóst is alkotmánybírónak jelöli a Tisza Párt Belföld frissítve Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Ligeti Miklóst, a Transparency International magyarországi jogi igazgatóját is alkotmánybírónak jelöli a Tisza Párt – jelentette be Magyar Péter miniszterelnök a Facebook-oldalán . A bejegyzés szerint a Tisza öt új alkotmánybírót jelöl, akik a következők: Dr. Chronowski Nóra – egyetemi tanár, az MTA doktora, alkotmányjogász; Dr. Ligeti Miklós – jogvédő, büntetőjogász, a Transparency International magyarországi jogi igazgatója; Dr. Kovács András György – kúriai tanácselnök bíró, PhD fokozattal rendelkező közigazgatási jogász; Dr. Orosz Árpád Gábor – a Kúria Polgári Kollégiumának egykori vezetője, tanácselnök bíró polgári jogász, európai jogi szakjogász, 1993 óta a Szegedi Tudományegyetem oktatója; Dr. Szomora Zsolt – a Szegedi Tudományegyetem Állam- és Jogtudományi Kar Bűnügyi Tudományok intézetének helyettese, habilitált egyetemi tanár. Magyar Péter szerint az ígéretükhöz híven olyan jelölteket javasoltak alkotmánybírónak, akik nemcsak az Alaptörvény előírásainak, de minden más szakmai követelménynek megfelelnek. „Az utóbbi hetekben számos kiváló jogásszal egyeztettünk. Feddhetetlenség, integritás, függetlenség és valódi szakmai teljesítmény, ezeket a szempontokat mérlegeltük. Figyelemmel voltunk továbbá arra is, hogy valamennyi jogterületet lefedjenek a jelöltek: alkotmányjog, büntetőjog, közigazgatási jog, polgári jog és alapjogok” – írta a miniszterelnök. A jelöltek bizottsági meghallgatására hétfőn kerül sor, az Országgyűlés pedig kedden délelőtt választja meg az öt új alkotmánybírót. Az Alkotmánybíróság új tagjait titkos szavazással választják meg. Az alkotmánybíráknál az Alaptörvény 17. módosításával visszaállították a 70 éves felső korhatárt, és ezzel megszűnt a hetven év feletti Polt Péter és három másik alkotmánybíró megbízatása. Polt mellett Haszonicsné Ádám Mária, Juhász Miklós és Lomnici Zoltán mandátuma szűnt meg szeptember 1-jén. Novemberben jár le Czine Ágnes alkotmánybírónak, a testület elnökhelyettesének a 12 éves megbízatása. Egy alkotmánybíró, Hende Csaba – korábbi MDF-es, majd fideszes képviselő, honvédelmi miniszter – már júliusban távozott a 15 tagú testületből, a tizenhetedik alaptörvény-módosítás és az alkotmánybírósági törvény szabályainak következtében, helyére Sonnevend Pált , az ELTE Állam- és Jogtudományi Karának tanszékvezető egyetemi tanárát, korábbi dékánját választotta alkotmánybírónak az Országgyűlés. A bírók megbízatásának hosszát a tizenhetedik alaptörvény-módosítás 12-ről 9 évre csökkentette. Ligeti Miklós, a Transparency International Magyarország jogi igazgatója korábban pályázott a Nemzeti Vagyonvisszaszerzési és Vagyonvédelmi Hivatal (NVVH) elnöki pozíciójára is, ám arra végül Unger Anna politológust választották meg. Arra a kérdésre, hogy hogyan élte meg, hogy – a várakozásokkal ellentétben – mégsem ő lett az NVVH elnöke, azt felelte: „Nincsenek érzelmeim, és nincs lelkiállapotom.” Szerinte nem is lenne elegáns bármit is mondania .
